first_impression.reaction: Sophie here. I Googled this because my claw setting keeps catching on my ski gloves and we're about to choose wedding bands. The opening line, 'This one asks what happens on a ski lift, a reef dive and a long-haul flight', is exactly my situation, and there's no 'dream ring' fluff. I skimmed the takeaways, then read the bezel, claw, channel and travel sections properly. I skipped the stone hardness bit.

journey.quote: Tension, channel and bar settings can be hard or even impossible to resize, so confirm the size before you order.
journey.reaction: Useful straight away. We're choosing bands now, and my fingers swell in heat, so this is a real trade-off and not just filler.

journey.quote: Skip it if: maximum sparkle is the point. A bezel covers more of the edge than claws and lets in slightly less light.
journey.reaction: I like that every setting gets a 'skip it if'. It reads like advice, not a sales pitch.

journey.quote: Compass-set is a style variation, with four claws at 12, 3, 6 and 9 o'clock rather than at the corners. Choose it for the look, not as a safety feature.
journey.reaction: Honest. A jeweller would have upsold me on that.

journey.section: Before a destination wedding: claw check and insurance
journey.quote: Book a setting check four to six weeks before you fly, so any re-tipping or tightening is done with time to spare.
journey.reaction: This is the one line I'd actually put in the calendar. It's the first moment the page feels like it's thinking about our wedding, not just my ring.

journey.section: From the ring to the adventure
journey.quote: A ring chosen for the trail often comes with a wedding in the same spirit: a mountain lodge, a coastline, a long weekend that runs into the honeymoon.
journey.reaction: Bit of a stretch from claws to mountain lodges. Not tacky, but I can see the turn to the sales bit coming.

journey.section: From the ring to the adventure
journey.quote: Wedded Concierge plans venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world, with one Wedded Advisor as your single point of contact from start to finish.
journey.reaction: One person from start to finish is what I want. But every planner says end-to-end. Nothing on this page shows me what that actually means for guest travel or a real wedding they've done.

unanswered_questions: Does the Wedded Advisor help with anything ring- or band-related before the trip (insurance, carrying rings through customs, who holds the rings on the day), or is this just a jewellery article?
What does 'plans venue, travel, vendors and payments' include for 60 to 90 guests, half flying internationally? Do you handle guest flights and transfers?
Is there a real wedding, with venue and date, for an outdoorsy couple like the 'mountain lodge, a coastline' one described?
would_share_with: James: the channel and travel band sections, since we're picking wedding bands
Not Mum and Dad; nothing here for them

cta_reaction.quote: Talk to a Wedded Concierge about a wedding abroad
cta_reaction.why: It's low-pressure, which I like. But I came for ring advice, and one paragraph isn't enough to make me hand over our wedding. I'd click 'browse destination wedding locations by region' first, and enquire only after a couple of planning posts and a real wedding.

top_3_changes: Bridge to the wedding with something practical instead of 'a ring chosen for the trail often comes with a wedding in the same spirit', for example who carries and insures the rings when you fly to your own wedding.
Link one real wedding with venue and date (an outdoor or adventurous one) near the CTA so 'start to finish' has proof.
Add one line on wedding bands for active couples matching an engagement ring, since that's the decision couples like us are making at this stage.

checks.check: Every journey point and the CTA reaction has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Sophie & James (Sydney, early research, 14 months out, active, wary of 'end-to-end' claims)
No invented brand facts; anything the page doesn't say is listed in unanswered_questions
[[VERIFY]] markers and HTML comments ignored as invisible
Didn't invent problems; no turn-offs found, positives recorded where earned

assumptions: Assumed Sophie is already engaged and searching because of snagging and the wedding band choice, since the persona is 14 months out from the wedding.
